A_target.statement:
Let $X > 0$ be a [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] with $\map \Pr {X > t} \in \openint 0 1$ for some $t$.
Then $\map \Pr {X > s + t \mid X > s} = \map \Pr {X > t}$ for all $s, t \ge 0$ {{iff}} $X$ has an [[Definition:Exponential Distribution|exponential distribution]].

B_source.statement:
Let $X$ take values in $\set {1, 2, \ldots}$.
Then $\map \Pr {X > m + n \mid X > m} = \map \Pr {X > n}$ for all $m, n$ {{iff}} $X$ is [[Definition:Geometric Distribution|geometric]], with $\map \Pr {X > n} = \map \Pr {X > 1}^n$.

derived.S(m + n) = S(m) S(n) on integers: S(s + t) = S(s) S(t) on [0, infinity)

object_map.reformulation: Pass from integer to real times: the multiplicative functional equation for the survival function forces an exponential, using monotonicity to fill in irrational times.

validity_conditions: Right-continuity and monotonicity of the survival function replace the discreteness used in the geometric case.
The non-degeneracy condition excludes S identically 0 or 1.
proof_plan:
Let $\map S t = \map \Pr {X > t}$.
Memorylessness is equivalent to $\map S {s + t} = \map S s \map S t$.
As in the source result, induction gives $\map S n = \map S 1^n$, and $\map S {1 / n}^n = \map S 1$ gives $\map S q = \map S 1^q$ for rational $q > 0$.

By the non-degeneracy assumption, $0 < \map S 1 < 1$; let $\lambda = -\ln \map S 1 > 0$.
As $S$ is decreasing and right-continuous, $\map S t = e^{-\lambda t}$ for all real $t \ge 0$.
